chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hisham ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah or to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'When a man buys a slave girl who has not yet reached puberty, or who has despaired of menstruation,' he said: 'There is no harm in not clearing her womb.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istibra' for a pre-pubescent or menopausal female slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal ruling of 'istibra'' (confirming non-pregnancy) for a purchased female slave, establishing that waiting for one menstrual cycle is not obligatory if she is pre-pubescent or menopausal. This ruling is derived from the principle that the primary purpose of istibra' is to ascertain lineage and avoid uncertainty, which is naturally absent in these two specific physiological states. It highlights the practical application of fiqh principles regarding the status of concubines in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Haris, from Abdullah Bin Amro who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> or to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The slave girl whom the man buys, and she has yet to be an adult, or has despaired from the menstruation’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if he does not clear her womb’.
